newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF-COLES TAKES SURPRISE LEAD IN DUTCH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-COLES TAKES SURPRISE LEAD IN DUTCH OPEN.

text.p: Former market stall trader Robert Coles took a surprise lead after the first round of the Dutch Open on Thursday.
The 24-year-old Briton, in his second year on the European Tour, powered to within a stroke of the course record in a seven-under-par 64, two better than his previous career-best.
It left him a stroke ahead of three other players, two of them more seasoned professionals from England, David Gilford and Roger Chapman, who are both bidding for Ryder Cup places.

Gilford lies 19th in the current Cup standings and believes "one and a bit wins" from a possible six events left to count, including this week, will earn him his Valderrama place against the U.S. Chapman is 20th.
Another surprise challenger from Britain, Miles Tunnicliff, picked up three shots in the last three holes in gathering dusk to join them in second place.
While Gilford's round was steady as he built his challenge on four birdies at regular intervals over his opening nine, Chapman surged into contention in spectacular fashion.
He birdied six of the first seven holes. After a slight decline he also finished with a flourish with a seven-foot putt for an eagle at the 18th.
Australian Wayne Riley prevented British players having it all their own way. His 66 matched that of Scotland's Paul Lawrie to put the pair in a share of fifth place.
Italy's Costantino Rocca and Scot Sam Torrance have most reason to crave success this week with most of their direct rivals absent.

Rocca, ninth in the Ryder Cup points table, had a 68 for his best day for several weeks after suffering an injury to his side which caused him to withdraw from the U.S. Open and slump from third in the rankings.
"I'm wearing an elastic support around my ribs which stops me turning freely," said Rocca, who is bidding for his third successive Cup appearance.
"But this was encouraging and if the injury continues to improve and I don't get any more injuries then maybe I can make the team."
Torrance, though, will have to battle hard to make the cut after deciding to soldier on despite a chest muscle injury. He shot 74.
